title: Rabin-Karp Search
statement: Return the first index of `pattern` in `text`, or -1 when it is absent. The rolling-hash search computes the hash of the pattern and of every window of the same length. A hash hit still checks the characters, so a collision cannot cause a false match.
hints: A polynomial hash treats the string as digits in a large base, modulo a prime.
The next window drops the outgoing character, multiplies by the base, and adds the incoming character.
Equal hashes are only a candidate. Compare the slice before returning the index.
editorial: Hash the pattern and the first window. The multiplier of the outgoing character is base^(m-1) modulo the prime, precomputed with fast exponentiation. Slide one character at a time. When the hashes agree and the characters agree, return that index. If the pattern is longer than the text, return -1. An empty pattern matches at index 0.
